Initial Psychiatric Evaluation
Three Rivers Behavioral Health Associates - 4100 Penn Avenue, Suite 6, Pittsburgh, PA 15224
Patient	Jonah R. Castellanos-Meyer
Date of birth	12 Jan 1992
MRN	TRB-204417
SSN	xxx-xx-9960
Insurance	Keystone Unified Health Plan, ID KUH88120447
Date of evaluation	October 21, 2026
Evaluator	Priyanka Subramaniam, MD

Reason for referral
Mr. Castellanos-Meyer is a 34-year-old bus operator for the Allegheny Steel City Transit Authority referred by his primary care physician, Dr. Owen Blackfeather, after two weeks of sleeping three hours a night followed by a period in which he "could not get off the couch." He is on leave and asks for FMLA paperwork.
History of present illness
He describes at least four episodes since his early twenties of elevated mood, little need for sleep, rapid speech and overspending lasting four to six days. In the most recent, in early September, he put $9,200 on a credit card in one weekend, mostly on camera equipment. These are followed by weeks of low mood. Current PHQ-9 is 17. He denies suicidal intent but has had passive thoughts ("it would be easier not to wake up"). No psychosis.
Past psychiatric history
One hospitalization, Monongahela Valley Hospital, March 3-9, 2019, after an overdose of sleeping pills. Discharged on sertraline, which he says "made everything faster." No outpatient follow-up since 2020.
Substance use
Drinks most evenings, four to six beers, more on days off. AUDIT-C is 9. He was arrested for DUI in August 2022 (off duty, personal vehicle; license suspended 60 days; the Authority was notified). Uses cannabis edibles to sleep. Denies other drugs.
Family and social history
Mother, Ruth Meyer, has Huntington's disease; he has declined predictive genetic testing and says that not knowing is "the only way I can drive a bus." Father's side: an uncle with "manic depression." Raised Jehovah's Witness, no longer practicing, and estranged from most of his mother's family over it.
He lives with his partner of six years, Marcus Tolliver, in Bloomfield. He identifies as gay; out at home, not at work. Marcus is the emergency contact (412.555.0139) and came to the first half of the visit with the patient's consent. He is a steward in ATU Local 85 and worries a diagnosis will be used against him in a pending grievance.
Mental status examination
Casually dressed, cooperative, good eye contact. Speech normal rate today. Mood "flat." Affect constricted. Thought process linear. Insight fair. Judgment fair.
Assessment
Bipolar II disorder, current episode depressed, moderate (DSM-5-TR; F31.81)
Alcohol use disorder, moderate (F10.20)
Family history of Huntington's disease; neurologic exam unremarkable today
Plan
Start lamotrigine 25 mg daily, titrate per schedule; rash precautions reviewed. Taper sertraline over two weeks.
No driving for work until re-evaluated. Leave certified through November 30, 2026; form sent to the Authority's leave office, attention file LV-2026-0733, with diagnosis withheld.
Referral to intensive outpatient program for alcohol use. He agreed to remove the 9 mm handgun from the home; Marcus will take it to his brother's.
Safety plan completed. Return 11/04/2026. Crisis line reviewed.
P. Subramaniam, MD - DEA FS4471900 - License MD-448120 - CPT 90792
